newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea protesters clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea protesters clash with police.

text.p: An anti-government protest in Papua New Guinea erupted into violence on Wednesday after demonstrators broke loose from the crowd and started looting nearby shops.

A Reuters eyewitness reported that about 200 demonstrators, from a total of around 1,500, clashed with police after starting to loot two supermarkets. Police fired tear gas into the crowd and live ammunition into the air to calm the situation.

The protesters gathered by Port Moresby's Murray barracks to demand the reinstatement of army chief Jerry Singirok, dismissed after demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan over the use of foreign mercenaries against an island uprising.

About 300 police, some wearing bullet-proof vests, blocked off the street where the protesters gathered and officers said they would not let the demonstrators march on parliament house as was planned.
Soldiers, confined to barracks since the South Pacific nation's crisis began on Monday, did not get involved.
Police officers said the demonstrators, who were chanting "We want Chan, we want Chan", were hoping to deliver a protest petition to a government minister and would then be told to disperse.
